title: Short Stuff: Jigsaw Puzzles
summary: Short Stuff episode on jigsaw puzzles. The hosts open with casual banter about enjoying puzzles and a college puzzle weekend. They trace the origin to John Spilsbury, a mid-1700s English engraver and mapmaker who in 1766 cut a map into pieces as a geography teaching tool, and note how puzzles later became marketing giveaways. They discuss Kodak's self-described "world's largest" puzzle, larger record-setting puzzles (a 2018 Dubai Year of Zayed puzzle and a half-million-piece lotus puzzle in Ho Chi Minh City), and challenge puzzles such as the nine-piece Ice Puzzle Nine by designer Osaka, with a video of Chris Ramsey solving it in about two hours and a Puzzle Guy video of the harder Puzzle Twenty Nine. They cover Dave Evans of Dorset, England, whose giant hand-cut wooden puzzle collapsed during filming and was rebuilt, rival collectors of over a thousand puzzles each, a 2019 human jigsaw puzzle of over 1,700 people for autism awareness, and a Simpsons donkey-puzzle gag. Ad-free; sign-off near the end.

segments.title: Opening banter about puzzles
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about whether they enjoy jigsaw puzzles and recall a college puzzle weekend.

segments.title: Origin of jigsaw puzzles
segments.summary: Sir John Spilsbury, an English engraver and mapmaker, is credited in 1766 with creating the first jigsaw puzzle by cutting a map into country pieces to teach geography. Puzzles then spread as home entertainment and marketing giveaways.

segments.title: Kodak's 'world's largest' puzzle
segments.summary: The hosts question Kodak's claim that its roughly 51-piece, large-format puzzle is the world's largest, and note that much larger puzzles exist.

segments.title: Record-setting giant puzzles
segments.summary: A 2018 Dubai puzzle honoring the Year of Zayed, about 66,000 square feet, and a Ho Chi Minh City puzzle of over half a million pieces forming a lotus flower are described as far bigger records.
topics: Ho Chi Minh City lotus puzzle

segments.title: Challenge puzzles: Ice Puzzle Nine and Puzzle Twenty Nine
segments.summary: Small but very hard puzzles by designer Osaka are discussed. Ice Puzzle Nine has nine pieces in a small tray and Chris Ramsey solved it in about two hours. Puzzle Twenty Nine has five corner pieces, identical colors, and is much harder, as shown in a video by the Puzzle Guy.

segments.title: Dave Evans' collapsed wooden puzzle
segments.summary: Dave Evans of Dorset, England, built a huge hand-cut wooden puzzle, certified as a record, which collapsed during filming. He spent sixteen days rebuilding it with assistants.

segments.title: Puzzle collection records
segments.summary: Two record-seekers, Louisa Figueredo of Brazil and Georgina Gil Lacuna of the Philippines, each have over a thousand puzzles and trade the title. The hosts joke about bequests and hand-me-down puzzles.

segments.title: Largest human jigsaw puzzle
segments.summary: In March 2019, more than 1,700 people formed a human jigsaw puzzle piece, the Autism Speaks symbol, to raise autism awareness, and Guinness recognized it as a largest human image record. A Simpsons donkey-puzzle gag closes the topic.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck wrap up the episode and thank listeners.
